narrative.overview:
The masterclass is presented as a limited institutional edition: a printed prospectus you are invited into. Every screen is set on warm bone stock or an ink gallery plate, divided by hairline rules, with one burnished copper used as ink rather than paint. There is no chrome, no glass, no floating UI: type, rule and live data carry the whole composition.

The ornament is real information. A 150-cell admission ledger replaces every progress bar and shows confirmed, held and open seats from the live API. A tilted ivory admission pass with a perforated stub, serial number, seal and barcode stands in for the photograph the project does not have. Motion is arrival, not decoration, and collapses to stillness under prefers-reduced-motion.

The two refused worlds are explicit: the dark-gradient, neon-badge crypto-conference template, and the soft cream-and-terracotta invitation tier with rounded panels and script faces.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-black gallery plates alternating with bone paper; hairline rules instead of cards.
One burnished copper, used as ink (datelines, italic accent, held seats, seal, focus).
Bodoni Moda display with true italics, Archivo running text, DM Mono for data.
Square corners on every surface; circles only where the object is circular.
Perforated ticket geometry: dashed seams, punched notches, stamped seal, barcode.
A live 150-cell admission ledger as the signature artifact, full-bleed at every width.
Mobile-first, bilingual EN/SW, WCAG 2.2 AA, reduced-motion safe.
Async waits drawn as press proofs: labelled status rules and structural skeletons, never shimmer.
A missing address becomes a struck record: an oversized 404 over a printed record-check docket.

rules.name: The One Copper Rule
rules.body: Copper never becomes a field of colour. It appears as ink on at most 5% of a viewport - a dateline, one word, a held cell, a seal, a focus ring - and only as a fill for hover states and the held seat state. Its rarity is what makes it read as value.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px, never with weight: 0.18 alpha for dividers, 0.36 for control edges, 0.47 when the line itself carries meaning. Decorative borders thicker than 1px do not exist; the only 2px stroke is the copper focus outline.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure white and no pure black. Paper is #f2ede3, ink is #14120e, and every neutral sits on the same warm hue so the page reads as stock and pressed ink, not screen white.

rules.name: The Three-Line Rule
rules.body: The hero lockup never exceeds three lines at any viewport, and never splits one word's scale from another's. One line may be italic; one word may be copper; never both in the same word.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: DM Mono is reserved for data, keys, numerals and micro-labels. Sentences, ledes and FAQ answers are always Archivo. If a run of text needs to be read as prose, it is not monospace.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces have no shadow at rest. If a new element needs to lift, it changes tone or gains a hairline - it does not gain a drop shadow. The admission pass is the only exception and it stays one.

rules.name: The Proofing Rule
rules.body: No wait is a blank panel or an unlabelled spinner. Every wait names the process and shows the structure of what is coming; the travelling copper rule is the only continuous animation permitted on paper and it freezes under reduced motion without hiding the status.

dos: Do set every section on a tonal plate (paper, paper-sunk or ink) divided by a 1px hairline, with clamp(4rem, 8vw, 7.5rem) vertical rhythm.
Do use the 150-cell ledger wherever seats are counted, including payment summaries and admin views, in paper or on-ink tone.
Do set dates, serials, prices, statuses and micro-labels in DM Mono uppercase, and keep sentences in Archivo.
Do keep copper to at most 5% of a viewport and reserve the copper-light step for dark grounds.
Do keep every corner square and every edge a 1px hairline; reserve circles for the seal, notches, radio and spinner.
Do localise both languages fully (EN/SW, SW default) and keep the three-line hero lockup intact in both.
Do preserve the existing prices, dates, contacts, FAQ answers and booking behaviour.
donts: Don't introduce gradients, glows, glass, backdrop blur, pill radii, or floating cards with drop shadows.
Don't wrap content in nested cards or add a card where a hairline rule and a heading will do.
Don't use copper as a background wash, badge colour, or decorative block; it is ink, not paint.
Don't use monospace for prose, or uppercase Bodoni for body copy.
Don't hide the mobile navigation behind a hamburger; keep the nav row visible.
Don't invent photography, speakers, testimonials, logos or press marks; the pass, seal, barcode and ledger are the only imagery.
Don't add a fourth typeface or a second accent colour.
